subject: Intermittent silent chunks causing degraded throughput — renewal at risk
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@aurelia-systems.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent silent chunks observed on L2 streaming endpoints — urgent

Hi Neha,

We started seeing repeated 10–20s silent windows in the streaming responses from your L2 endpoints this morning. During the gaps tokens stop arriving; client-side shows a WebSocket STATUS 0 then resumes. Throughput to our service dropped ~30% and we observed a simultaneous spike in 5xxs from the gateway (attached session trace).

Impacted behavior:
- Streaming chunk gaps (10–20s) on ~5% of active sessions during peak.
- Client reconnects or sees long silence before final token.
- End-to-end latency increases and throughput falls; our batch ingestion backs up.

We collected a session trace and a short pcap and attached them — please review. This is on a production path we depend on and our renewal (May 14) is getting flagged internally because of the business impact.

Can your team confirm receipt and propose next steps? We can be on a call in the next hour if that's helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah
S. Lee
Head of Platform
Aurelia Systems

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-03T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Initial findings — proxy/NLB interaction + KV cache hints

Quick reproducibility work and initial notes after loading the session trace into our dev harness.

What we observed:
- Reproducer shows token emission pauses that coincide with upstream keepalive resets on the edge proxy layer. Nginx shows a flurry of "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header" and TCP FINs in the same windows.
- AWS NLB metrics show client-side idle periods aligning with the silence windows; default idle-timer (350s) doesn’t map cleanly but we see periodic connection resets at the proxy layer synchronized with internal autoscaler events.
- KV cache invalidation for a small set of customer prefixes occurred during their peak, causing miss storms for a subset of requests (amplifies latency when the model warms KV cache).

Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- Increase socket-level heartbeat from 10s -> 5s for affected route (reduces silent detection time).
- Route Aurelia sessions to a less-loaded pool and temporary model-variant (lower mem footprint) to avoid KV thrash.
- Patch nginx upstream read-timeout and increase buffer sizes for chunked transfer.

Logs referenced: nginx-proxy-stdout-20280403.log (attached). Sample excerpt:

--- LOG EXCERPT ---
[2028-04-01T11:03:14Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: l2.edge.redwood, request: "POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1"
[2028-04-01T11:03:14Z] 502 from upstream id=0x3f
--- END EXCERPT ---

Next steps:
- I’ll run a controlled test tomorrow (04/04) targeting the affected pool and validate mitigation impact.
- If mitigations fail, we escalate to arch and ops for a hot rollback and may need a short maintenance window.

David
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference
Attachment: nginx-proxy-stdout-20280403.log

This is still visible in our customer telemetry and has been flagged to our product and procurement teams. Given the proximity of our renewal, they asked me to request formal exec engagement from Redwood: a named executive to confirm we have a timebound plan and to discuss potential short-term credits if incidents continue.

We appreciate the mitigation work so far. Please let us know who from your exec team can be on a call today (we're flexible).

—Sarah

Date: 2028-04-08T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Exec ping requested by Aurelia — board/renewal at risk (summary & ask)

Folks — Aurelia asked for exec-level engagement today; they tied continued intermittent silent chunks to an internal renewal review. Below is a concise summary and asks for leadership:

Impact summary:
- Symptom: intermittent silent-token windows (10–20s) during streaming affecting throughput and E2E latency.
- Scope: peaked at ~5% sessions on worst day; current residual ~1% after routing mitigations.
- Business impact: ingestion backlog at Aurelia, product & procurement involvement, renewal date 2028-05-14.

Technical status (short):
- Root cause hypothesis: edge proxy + autoscaler interactions triggering upstream closes and amplifying KV cache warm misses. Patch & routing mitigations reduced but did not eliminate.

Immediate asks for execs/leadership approval:
1) Approve a customer-facing credit at the level of 6% of monthly invoice if the issue persists beyond 72 hours post-mitigation (pre-approved template attached to the comms DOC).
2) Approve a one-hour maintenance window for a hot rollback/patch if our full mitigation test tomorrow reproduces the silence.
3) Rishi: coordinate a leadership intro call with Aurelia (their execs want a named contact).

I recommend exec sponsorship from VP-Sales and VP-Engineering to reassure the account. If we confirm continued silences after the next test, I will request an official exec introduction with suggested language.

Quote from customer (their most recent):
> This is still visible in our customer telemetry and has been flagged to our product and procurement teams. Given the proximity of our renewal, they asked me to request formal exec engagement from Redwood.

Please confirm approval or propose adjustments. I will prepare the customer-facing one-pager and a proposed credit figure for legal.

—Neha
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
